subject: Re: Region pinning & data residency post-call recap and next steps
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@acmebank.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal <legal@acmebank.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Region pinning & data residency post-call recap and next steps

Hi Sanjay thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same picture.

Recap from today's discovery: 
- Requirement: EU-hosted data for EU customers and US-hosted data for US customers (data residency per customer/tenant).
- Failover: Acme asks about cross-region failover for availability while ensuring data residency constraints are honored.
- Backups: want encrypted backups that do not leave the originating region unless explicitly approved.
- Logs & audit: need audit logs for admin actions, with configurable retention and the ability to restrict log storage to the same region.
- PII handling: minimize storage of raw PII; need options for tokenization/redaction and clear retention controls.

What we can offer (high level):
- Region pinning: Available on Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted, customers can be pinned to a primary region (US/EU/APAC) and we publish SLOs per region.
- Cross-region failover: Supported but by default it uses an encrypted, metadata-first failover path. Customer data remains pinned; for failover we can route traffic to a compatible regional replica. Full cross-region replication of raw data is opt-in and requires explicit contract language (and optional CMK).
- Backups: Encrypted at rest and in transit. We support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). Backup replicas to a secondary region are off by default and can be enabled only with customer approval.
- Logs & retention: Retention is configurable. Default application logs retained 90 days; audit logs can be retained longer per contract. We can store logs in-region and provide tooling to export them to customer storage if required.
- PII controls: Redaction/tokenization at ingestion, field-level encryption, and selective retention policies. We can show example flows on a technical call.

Next steps / asks: 
1) Can you confirm the set of regions you need pinned per tenant (e.g., EU, US) and the expected traffic split?
2) Please list any endpoints you consider to carry PII so we can propose ingestion-level redaction.
3) Legal: who should we loop in for DPA review?
4) Technical deep-dive: propose a 60-min session next week with our infra team (Aditya) to go over failover mechanics and backup encryption.

I've attached a copy of our SOC 2 report and a simplified data flow diagram for your review.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0123

Attachments: SOC2_Report_Q1_2026.pdf (summary), redwood-data-flow-diagram.png

Thanks Rishi useful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- For failover: if we enable cross-region failover, will any customer data be replicated to the failover region at rest, or is it strictly a transient in-memory route? We need to understand RPO/RTO and whether failover writes create persistent copies in the DR region.
- Backups: we require that backups of EU tenants remain within EU unless Legal signs off and we have CMK in place. Can you confirm that replication to other regions is opt-in only?
- Logs: Can audit logs be configured to stay in-region and be exported to our S3 (EU) directly? If yes, what's the retention granularity?
- DPA: Legal wants to start a DPA review please route DPA and SOC docs to legal@acmebank.com.

Also, can Aditya join the technical call to walk through the failover path and KMS integration?

Sanjay
Sanjay Patel
VP, Cloud Platform Acme Bank

Sanjay thanks, noted. Answers inline: 

- Cross-region failover behavior: by default our failover route is metadata-based and will route traffic to a compatible regional replica that has customer data pinned. We do not create persistent copies in a secondary region unless the customer explicitly enables cross-region replication. In practice that means: transient routing and cached state allowed for availability; persistent replication of raw data requires opt-in and will be documented in the contract.
- RPO/RTO: Typical RTO for application-level failover is sub-minute for stateless requests; for stateful sessions we provide best-effort warm caches. If you need a formal RPO/RTO target (e.g., RPO 1h), we should capture that in the Dedicated/Private design and test via runbooks.
- Backups: Confirmed backups are encrypted and stored in-region by default. Cross-region backup replication is off by default and can only be enabled via change control and with CMK (customer-managed key) support.
- Logs & export: Audit logs can be stored in-region and we support push/export to customer-managed S3/GCS buckets. Retention is configurable by day (30/90/365+). We can provide an export connector to your EU S3; that will be included in the technical design.
- DPA & SOC: I've attached SOC2_Report_Q1_2026.pdf and the data flow diagram. We'll send the DPA template to legal@acmebank.com and loop our privacy counsel as needed.

Proposed next step: Tech deep-dive with Aditya and our infra team. Aditya can you run through the failover path, KMS flow, and backup replication options? I propose 60 minutes next Tue/Wed (Oct 13/14) 9-11am PT. Sanjay which slot works for you?

Thanks,
Rishi

- A short list of endpoints you consider to carry PII (e.g., /chat/completions, /uploads, /events) and typical payload sizes/requests per second.
- Your desired RPO/RTO targets for critical tenants.
- Any compliance constraints (e.g., specific EU country localization, additional encryption certifications).

1) Failover architecture and flow (how region pinning + transient caches work)
2) Backup lifecycle and CMK integration (KMS flows + key rotation)
3) Audit/log export and retention configuration (how to push to your EU S3)
4) PII ingestion patterns and our redaction/tokenization options
